olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Among positive integers expressible as sums of 2005 consecutive integers, which is in the 2005th position when listed in order?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2005

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Show that $a^2b^2+b^2c^2+3b^2-c^2-a^2=2005$ has no integer solutions.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2005

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: In $\triangle ABC$, $P,Q,R$ are where the incircle touches $AB,BC,CA$. $L,M,N$ are the feet of altitudes of $\triangle PQR$ from $R,P,Q$. (a) Show $AN,BL,CM$ meet at a point. (b) Show this point lies on the line joining the orthocenter and circumcenter of $\triangle PQR$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2005

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Red and Blue alternate choosing rows/columns of a $10\times 10$ board (Blue first), coloring them in their color (overwriting). After 20 turns, Red wins if Red squares exceed Blue by $\geq 10$. Who wins?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2005

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: In $\triangle ABC$, $H$ = orthocenter, $M$ = midpoint of $AC$. Let $\ell$ be the line through $M$ parallel to the bisector of $\angle AHC$. Prove $\ell$ divides the triangle into two parts of equal perimeter.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2005

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $n$ cards numbered $1,\ldots,n$; $p$ boxes. Distribute cards so each box has the same sum. Find all $n$ for which this is possible for a fixed prime $p$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2005
